chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) inquired about a man while I was in his presence, so it was said to him: 'Poverty has afflicted him.' He said: 'So what is he doing today?' It was said: 'He is at home worshipping his Lord.' He said: 'So from where is his livelihood?' It was said: 'From one of his brothers (in faith).' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By God! The one who provides his livelihood is a more devoted worshiper than he.'

key_terms.إِخْوَان: Brothers in faith — fellow believers who owe mutual support and solidarity to one another
key_terms.الْحَاجَة: Neediness, poverty — the state of being dependent on others due to lack of means
key_terms.عِبَادَة: Worship, devotion — any act of obedience to God performed with intention, not limited to ritual prayer
key_terms.قُوت: Sustenance, livelihood, daily provision — what is sufficient to live on

ai.seo_question: Is working for one's livelihood considered worship in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) used a real-life scenario to overturn a common pietistic assumption: that withdrawing from work in favor of exclusive worship is the highest form of devotion. In the early Islamic community, some believed that leaving worldly labor to dedicate oneself entirely to prayer was spiritually superior. The Imam emphatically rejected this view, declaring by oath that the brother who actively earns and supports the worshiping man outranks him in worship — because productive work for oneself and one's dependents is itself a form of 'ibadah when performed with the right intention.
